summary: This program builds two sets of song titles \u2014 yours and a friend's \u2014 and uses Java's Set operations to work out which songs you share, what a combined playlist would look like, and which songs are yours alone.

lines.text: A Set is the right collection here because a playlist of titles has no duplicates, and set-to-set comparison methods come built in. A HashSet keeps no particular order, so the titles may print in a different order than you added them.

Passing myTitles to the constructor makes a copy of your playlist. Every comparison below works on a fresh copy, because these operations change the set they are called on and you do not want to damage the original.
retainAll throws away anything that is not also in the friend's playlist, leaving only the songs you have in common.
addAll pours the friend's titles into the copy of yours, giving the single road-trip playlist. Because it is a Set, "Respect" appears once rather than twice \u2014 the duplicate is silently dropped.
removeAll strips out every shared title, leaving the songs only you have. Direction matters: swap the two sets and you would instead get the friend's songs that are new to you.
